title: Oncall heuristics for transient signal bursts
body:
Summary:
This note collects practical heuristics for oncall engineers to triage and mitigate short-lived/low-impact alert storms ("transient signal bursts"). These bursts are the single biggest source of wasted attention for our oncall teams right now: they spike noise, obscure real degradations, and increase rework (flip-flop changes to alert thresholds). The goal is to give a lightweight decision framework: when to silence/mute, when to escalate, and when to record and ignore.

Scope and definitions:
- Transient signal burst: sudden increase in alert rate for a rule or related set of rules that returns to baseline within 5–60 minutes without manual remediation.
- Burst cause examples: momentary downstream dependency outage, noisy metric emitter, rollout-related telemetry gap, autoscaler thrash, brief infra maintenance window.
- Out-of-scope: sustained SLO burn (>1h) or customer-facing errors with clear impact (error pages, API error surface increase >2%).

Why this matters (empirical):
- Median noise-induced pager wakeups per week increased ~30% over last quarter (see linked artifacts).
- In several recent incidents, teams applied short-lived threshold changes and later reverted them, creating config churn and regression risk.

Heuristics quick reference (one-page):
1) First 3 alerts in <2 minutes on same rule: assume "burst" unless accompanied by customer complaints or metric gaps in upstream/downstream.
2) Check customer-facing signals within 2 min window: if user-facing metrics are flat, deprioritize escalation.
3) Correlate with deploys/rollouts in last 30 minutes (git tags, CI/CD dashboard). If correlated, flag as rollout-noise.
4) Check metric emission patterns: sudden periodic gap/restore often indicates exporter restart — use "metric-liveness" panel.
5) Apply a short temporary mute (10–30 min) for noisy alerts after confirming no user impact and after notifying owners.
6) If alerts persist beyond 30 minutes or reappear after mute, escalate and run deeper investigation.

Playbook for immediate oncall actions:
- Step 0: Acknowledge the page and add a short note in the incident channel: "observed burst, triaging via heuristics v1 — checking customer surface and recent deploys".
- Step 1: Quickly check 3 signals (target panels): API 5xx rate, global request latency p95, customer error pages. If any show real degradation, treat as full incident.
- Step 2: Check release activity: last 30–60 min deploys across services. If matched, tag as "likely rollout".
- Step 3: Query metric ingestion pipeline (prometheus-kafka consumer lag, exporter restarts). If ingestion gaps present, document and treat alerts as potentially spurious.
- Step 4: Communicate: post a short note in #sre-incidents and @team-oncall with action: mute candidate alerts (10m) + follow-up instructions.
- Step 5: Mute using scoped muting (service + rule) not global, and attach reason + expiry in the mute comment.
- Step 6: Observe for 10–30 minutes; if quiet, unmute and file a ticket for root cause analysis (SRE backlog).

Temporary-mute policy (recommended defaults):
- Allowed when: no user-facing impact detected AND cause likely telemetry or downstream flake AND owner is notified or owner oncall acknowledged.
- Duration: 10 minutes (short), 30 minutes (if burst is sustained but non-impacting).
- Escalation threshold: any recurrence after a mute or any sign of customer impact => immediate escalate.
- Muting must use the alerting system's scoped mute + include a link to the incident channel and a ticket ID if created.

When NOT to mute:
- Any increase in SLO burn rate >2% over baseline in last 5 minutes.
- Clear customer complaints or monitoring from the product team.
- Multiple independent alert classes tripping simultaneously (indicative of shared dependency outage).

Longer-term mitigations (post-incident):
- Add short-term de-dup window to high-cardinality rules: prefer 5–15s de-dup for noisy exporters.
- Adjust rule evaluation cadence for noisy metrics (e.g., 30s -> 60s) where latency cost acceptable.
- Implement circuit-breaker style suppression for flapping exporters: after N bursts in M minutes, escalate to pager once per X.
- Improve ingestion health dashboards (consumer lag, exporter process restart rate) and raise those as first-order alerts to separate telemetry health from product impact.
- Add synthetic traffic checks closer to user-facing SLOs to reduce reliance on noisy internal metrics.

Guidance for changing alert thresholds (PR checklist):
- Link to affected SLO or customer-facing metric.
- Show 90-day historical alert rate pre/post-proposed change (graph).
- Provide rollout plan: canary (10% of routes) -> monitor 24h -> full.
- Add rollback criteria and monitoring queries.
- Add owner and 48h follow-up ticket for observation.

Investigation examples (short-case studies):
- Example A (10/04/2024): Burst from exporter restarts on metrics-host-13 after kernel patching. Alert rule (exporter-up) fired 120 times in 8m. Action: scoped mute 20m, contacted infra team, infra rolled back kernel patch. Root cause: missing preflight check for exporter restart. Follow-up: add preflight and add exporter restart counter dashboard.
- Example B (12/20/2024): Autoscaler oscillation created CPU spikes across worker pool; internal readiness probes flapped which in turn triggered internal health alerts. Action: treated as valid degradation (customer p95+ increased); escalated. Follow-up: adjust autoscaler smoothing config.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should automatic suppression be before it masks real short outages? Current thinking: conservative by default — prefer human-in-the-loop for first 2 weeks of any new suppression rule.
- Ownership latency: muting requires owner-notify. What if owner is not reachable? Suggest SRE takes temp mute but files ticket and documents owner unreachability.

Practical notes to reviewers (Nora):
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive to reduce cognitive load during a pager storm.
- Need feedback from product teams on acceptable detection cadence changes for user-impacting signals.
- Propose a 6-week experiment: enable scoped muting defaults for non-customer-facing exporter rules and measure pager-lift.

Checklist for post-burst RCA ticket (minimal fields):
- Title, incident time window, burst rule(s), customer-impact (yes/no), temporary actions taken, owner, follow-up tasks (3), decision about threshold changes, expected rollout plan.

Slack/reference snippets to copy during an event:
- "Observed transient burst on <rule>. Checking customer surface and recent deploys. Muting scoped rule for 15m while we investigate. Will update in 10m."
- "Burst receded. Unmuted. Filing RCA: JIRA-SRE-###. Owner: infra. Next: add exporter restart counter."

Notes-to-self (TODO):
- Build 1-click mute workflow in internal alert UI that pre-fills duration and comment.
- Add a fast panel that correlates "deploys in last 60m" + "metric ingestion lag" for quicker triage.

End.
